title: Squad Atlas Onboarding (Payments)
description: Week-one essentials for a new engineer joining Squad Atlas, Meridian's payments squad — on-call, compliance, release policy, data handling, architecture, ownership, and secrets.

questions.prompt: Which tool does Squad Atlas use to run its on-call rotation and page the primary engineer?
questions.explanation: Atlas runs its on-call rotation through Opsgenie; alerts route to the primary engineer and escalate to secondary, then the squad lead (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook).

questions.prompt: How long does an Atlas on-call engineer have to acknowledge a page before Opsgenie escalates?
questions.explanation: Atlas's acknowledgement SLA is 10 minutes — miss it and Opsgenie escalates to the secondary, then to the squad lead (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook).

questions.prompt: On Squad Atlas, a failed payment settlement is classified as what incident severity?
questions.explanation: Severity is set by impact to money movement. A failed settlement impacts money movement, so it is always Sev1 — never downgraded to Sev2 because 'only a few payments' failed (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook).

questions.prompt: Because it handles cardholder data directly, Squad Atlas operates under which compliance regime?
questions.explanation: As Meridian's highest-volume card processor, Atlas operates under PCI-DSS Level 1 — the strictest tier — and every engineer completes PCI awareness training before production access (Squad Atlas — Compliance & Data Handling).

questions.prompt: How is card data classified under Meridian's data classification scheme on Squad Atlas?
questions.explanation: Card data is Tier 0 (Restricted), Meridian's highest tier. Tier 0 data may never be logged, never appear in error messages, and never leave services in PCI scope (Squad Atlas — Compliance & Data Handling).

questions.prompt: How does Squad Atlas handle the Primary Account Number (PAN) in its storage?
choices: Encrypted in place in the ledger
Tokenized at rest — the raw PAN is never persisted
Hashed with a salted SHA-256 digest
Stored only in an access-controlled audit table
questions.explanation: The PAN is tokenized at rest: the tokenization service exchanges it for a token at the edge, and only the token flows through Rail into Atlas datastores. A raw PAN found anywhere is a Tier 0 incident (Squad Atlas — Compliance & Data Handling).

questions.prompt: What does Squad Atlas's release policy say about deploy timing?
choices: No deploys after 5pm on any day
No deploys on Friday or over the weekend
Deploys allowed any time with one approval
questions.explanation: The pipeline is gated to refuse production releases Friday through Sunday — no Friday or weekend deploys. A fix that genuinely can't wait goes through the incident-change path, not the normal release (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy).

questions.prompt: How many approvals does a production change on Squad Atlas require?
choices: Dual approval — two engineers, one with context on the area
Three approvals including the squad lead
Approval from the on-call engineer only
questions.explanation: Every production change requires dual approval — two engineers — and one approver must have context on the area being changed; a rubber-stamp doesn't count (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy).

questions.prompt: Which check must pass before any Atlas pull request can merge?
questions.explanation: The ledger-reconciliation contract test must be green before merge — it verifies recorded entries match settled balances. A red result blocks merge with no override (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy).

questions.prompt: What is Squad Atlas's primary datastore?
questions.explanation: Atlas's primary datastore is Aurora PostgreSQL, chosen for strong consistency on balance reads and the durability money movement demands (Squad Atlas — Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: What is the name of the primary service Squad Atlas owns — the repo where the ledger, settlement workers, and reconciliation logic live?
questions.explanation: atlas-ledger-svc is Atlas's primary service and the codebase new hires should clone first — it holds the ledger, settlement workers, and reconciliation logic (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership; Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: What is the internal codename for Atlas's payment-initiation API?
questions.explanation: Rail is the internal name for the payment-initiation API on atlas-ledger-svc. 'Submit it to Rail' means the entry point that accepts a payment instruction and hands it to the ledger (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership; Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: Who is the squad lead and engineering manager of Squad Atlas?
questions.explanation: Priya Nair is Atlas's squad lead and EM — the escalation point for ownership disputes, hiring, and cross-squad commitments on the payment path. New hires book a week-one 1:1 with her (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership).

questions.prompt: Where does Squad Atlas store its secrets?
choices: AWS Secrets Manager, one secret per service
A shared org-wide Vault root path
questions.explanation: All Atlas secrets live in Vault under the dedicated per-squad namespace atlas/. Nothing belonging to Atlas is stored outside that namespace, and services read from atlas/ at runtime rather than copying secrets into code (Squad Atlas — Secrets & Access).

questions.prompt: What customer-facing SLA does Squad Atlas publish for payment status availability?
questions.explanation: Atlas publishes a customer-facing SLA of 99.95% monthly for payment status availability; breaching it triggers a customer-facing comms review (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership).
